about: Hydor's catalog of outside services an app can use: one where one is better overall, at most three otherwise, the first the default; with what each costs a small app (and the day it was read), its catches, and its keys as the keys card takes them. Providers' own pages; no figure that could not be read there. A step a provider's own page did not confirm is written {"unconfirmed": what} and shown as the link to it; a service with "hold" is left out until that line is taken away. Revisit each release.

needs.name: A database
needs.what: a place for the app's data when its server keeps no disk

builtIn.say: SQLite on the app's own disk: free, with nothing to sign up for. Choose a service only where the app has no disk (Cloudflare, Vercel, a host's free tier).

services.name: Neon
services.why: Plain Postgres, free with no card, and at its limit it stops writes rather than bill you.

free.text: 1 GB a project and 100 compute hours a month, no card

paid.text: By use, no minimum: $0.106 a compute hour and $0.35 a GB a month

services.catch: It sleeps after 5 minutes idle, so the first request after a pause waits.

keys.name: DATABASE_URL
keys.label: Connection address
keys.why: The app uses it to reach your database and save and read its information.
how: Go to console.neon.tech and sign in, making an account if you need one.
Click New Project, give it a name, pick the region closest to you, then click Create project.
On the project's main page, click Connect.
Copy the whole connection string shown. It contains your password, so share it only with this app.

services.name: Turso
services.why: SQLite as a service: code written for SQLite keeps working as it is.

free.text: 100 databases and 5 GB, 500 million rows read and 10 million written a month

paid.text: $4.99 a month

services.catch: It is not Postgres, and its pricing page does not say what happens past the free limit.

keys.name: TURSO_DATABASE_URL
keys.label: Database address
keys.why: The app uses it to find your database.
how: Go to app.turso.tech and sign up or sign in: databases and their access tokens are managed there.
Create a database and give it a name, or open one you already have.

how.unconfirmed: where the database's address is shown

looks.say: starts with libsql:// or turso:// and ends with turso.io

keys.name: TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN
keys.label: Database access token
keys.why: The app uses it to prove it is allowed to read and change your database.
how: At app.turso.tech, open the same database you took the address from.

how.unconfirmed: how to make a token there that may read and write

how: Paste the token into the app and keep it private.

leftOut.name: Supabase
leftOut.why: its free tier pauses a project after a week idle, and the next step is a big one

needs.name: Sending mail
needs.what: the mail an app sends people: sign-ups, notices, receipts

services.name: Resend
services.why: Needs no approval, and its free allowance fits a small app.

free.text: 3,000 mails a month, at most 100 a day

paid.text: $20 a month for 50,000

services.catch: You verify a domain of your own first, and an account whose mail people report as spam can be closed.

keys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
keys.label: Resend key
keys.why: The app uses it to send email through your Resend account.
how: Sign up at resend.com. To mail anyone but yourself you need a domain you own: without one, resend.dev reaches only your account's own address.
Open Domains, click Add Domain and enter your domain, or a part of it such as updates.yourdomain.com.
Copy the records Resend shows into the settings of the company where your domain is registered, exactly as written.
Return to Resend and verify. It often takes minutes but can take up to 72 hours.
Open API keys, click Create API Key, name it and choose Sending access.
Copy the key at once, because it is shown only one time.

services.name: Brevo
services.why: Also sends newsletters, from the same account.
services.catch: Brevo may hold a new account for review before it sends; you verify a sender or a domain there, and transactional mail is activated separately.

keys.name: BREVO_API_KEY
keys.label: Brevo key
keys.why: The app uses it to send email through your Brevo account.
how: Make an account at brevo.com and complete your profile on My profile: Brevo reviews accounts from it.
Open Settings, then Senders, Domains, IPs. Click Add a sender and save; if its domain is not authenticated, enter the 6-digit code Brevo emails there.
Under Domains, add a domain you own and follow the steps to authenticate it. Free addresses such as Gmail cannot be authenticated.
Open Settings, SMTP & API, API Keys & MCP, then Generate API key. Enter the verification code, name it, set expiry and access, and copy it: it is shown only once.
A key unused for 90 days is switched off. Transactional mail is activated separately: if sending is refused as not activated, ask Brevo to activate it.
After 30 days with no new address, Brevo refuses the key from a new one: if the server moves, allow its address under Settings, Security, Authorized IPs.

looks.say: starts with xkeysib- (not the separate SMTP key)

free.text: 300 emails a day

paid.text: $9 a month from 5,000 emails

services.name: Postmark
services.why: For mail that has to arrive: sign-in links, receipts.

free.text: 100 mails a month, for trying it

paid.text: $15 a month for 10,000

services.catch: Your account is approved by hand, usually within a day; until then it sends only to your own domains.

keys.name: POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN
keys.label: Postmark server token
keys.why: The app uses it to send email through your Postmark account.
how: Sign up at postmarkapp.com. A first server is made for you.
Open Sender Signatures and add the address you will send from, then click the link in the confirmation email. Or verify your whole domain.
For a domain, open its DNS Settings, copy the record shown to your domain company, then click Verify. Allow up to 48 hours.
Request approval in your account. Until approved, you can only send to your own verified domains. Review usually takes under a day on weekdays.
Open Servers, choose your server, open the API Tokens tab and copy the Server API token.

looks.say: a long string of random letters and numbers, from the server's API Tokens tab, not the account's

also.name: A mailbox you have
also.why: For a few mails a day, from your own address.
also.catch: Not for newsletters: Gmail stops at about 500 a day, and Microsoft 365 turns password sign-in off by default from the end of December 2026.
notFor: Cloudflare Workers: they cannot open the connection SMTP needs.

keys.name: SMTP_HOST
keys.label: Outgoing mail server
keys.why: The app uses it to know which server sends your email.
how: Look up your email provider's help page for its outgoing mail server, also called SMTP server.
For Gmail it is smtp.gmail.com, using port 587. There is no extra charge for an existing mailbox.
Outlook.com and Hotmail require a Microsoft sign-in method instead of a plain password, so they may not work here.

looks.say: a server name such as smtp.gmail.com

keys.name: SMTP_USER
keys.label: Email address
keys.why: The app uses it to sign in to your mailbox and send from it.
how: Use the mailbox you want the app's email to come from.
Type its full email address, including the part after the @ sign.
A personal Gmail may stop sending for up to a day after about 500 mails in one day.

keys.name: SMTP_PASSWORD
keys.label: App password
keys.why: The app uses it to sign in to your mailbox without your normal password.
how: For Gmail, first turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account.
Open Google's help page on app passwords and follow Create and manage your app passwords.
Create one for this app and copy the 16-digit passcode. Changing your Google password later cancels it.
No option? Work or school accounts, Advanced Protection, or security-key-only verification can hide it.
Microsoft 365 work mail: your administrator must allow Authenticated SMTP, and password sign-in is due to be off by default from end of December 2026.

looks.say: for Gmail, a 16-digit app passcode, not your normal password

leftOut.name: Amazon SES
leftOut.why: its approval and request signing are too hard for most people

leftOut.name: SendGrid
leftOut.why: there is no free plan any more

needs.name: A place to run
needs.what: where the app runs for other people

builtIn.say: Inside this Hydor: free, on this computer, signed in as you. Choose a service when other people use it.

services.name: DigitalOcean
services.why: A rented server that is easy to follow, in many regions.

paid.text: $12 a month for 2 GB of memory

services.catch: Backups cost extra, and a server switched off is still billed: delete it when you are done.
setup: Create a DigitalOcean account and add a payment method: servers cannot be made without one.
In Hydor, open the app's Launch tab and choose Add a server: it shows one line to paste.
In DigitalOcean, choose Create Droplet, a region near your users, Ubuntu and a size with 2 GB.
Under Authentication choose SSH Keys, add Hydor's line, then create the Droplet.
Copy its IP address into Hydor, compare the fingerprint it shows, and check the server.

clicks: Under “Choose a datacenter region”, pick the one nearest the people who will use your app.
Under “Choose an image” keep “Ubuntu”, and under “Choose a Droplet Plan” pick “Basic” with 2 GB of memory.
Under “Authentication”, open the “SSH Keys” tab and press “Add SSH Key”.
server.boxThen: Give it any name under “Key Name”, press “Add SSH Key”, then press “Create Droplet” at the bottom.
server.address: When it is ready, copy its “Public IPv4” address: four numbers shown beside its name, like 203.0.113.7.
server.compare: In DigitalOcean, open your new server and press “Web Console”. In the black window that opens, paste the line below and press Enter. Compare the code it writes with the one here.

clicks: Pick the nearest place under “Choose a datacenter region”, keep “Ubuntu” under “Choose an image”, and under “Choose a Droplet Plan” pick “Basic” with 2 GB of memory.
Under “Authentication”, choose “Password” and make up a long one. Hydor never needs it: the text switches signing in with it off.
Open “Additional Options”, switch on “Startup scripts”, paste the text into the box, then press “Create Droplet”.

services.name: Hetzner
services.why: About the cheapest server for the memory, in Europe.

paid.text: From €9.99 a month for 2 GB (CPX12, Helsinki), before VAT

services.catch: Hetzner restricts new cloud servers at the moment, for new customers among others, and its cheapest plans cannot be ordered: check before you count on it.
setup: Check first that Hetzner lets you order: it restricts new cloud servers at the moment.
Create an account with your details and a payment method, then open Hetzner Console and a project.
In Hydor, open the app's Launch tab and choose Add a server: it shows one line to paste.
In Hetzner, choose Add server: a location, Ubuntu, a size on offer, and Hydor's line as the SSH key.
Create it, copy its IP address into Hydor, compare the fingerprint, and check the server.

hold.name: Hetzner's servers
hold.why: new cloud servers cannot be ordered for now, as Hetzner has restricted them since June 2026, for new customers among others

services.name: Render
services.why: A platform with a disk: no server to look after.

paid.text: $25 a month for 2 GB, and $0.25 a GB of disk

services.catch: The free service has no disk and sleeps, so it cannot keep an app's data; each deploy of a service with a disk has a short outage.
setup: Create a Render account.
On the app's Launch tab choose Render: Hydor writes the platform's file and lists the steps.
On Render, connect the app's Git repository and choose a paid plan: a disk needs one.
Add the disk at the folder where the app keeps its data, then its keys as environment variables.
Deploy, and open the address Render gives.

leftOut.name: Fly.io
leftOut.why: a command-line tool and a card

needs.name: Web search
needs.what: searching the web from an app's AI features

services.name: Tavily
services.why: A free allowance each month, with no card.

free.text: 1,000 credits a month (a basic search is 1), no card

paid.text: $0.008 a credit, about $8 for 1,000 basic searches

services.catch: An advanced search counts as two.

keys.name: TAVILY_API_KEY
keys.label: Tavily search key
keys.why: The app uses it to search the web.
how: Go to app.tavily.com and sign in or make an account.
In your dashboard, find the API keys section. Click the + button if you want a new key just for this app.
Name it, choose a key type and, if you like, a monthly limit.
Copy the key and paste it into the app.

services.name: Exa
services.why: The lowest price a search, with a larger free allowance.

free.text: $10 of credit a month, about 2,500 light searches, no card

paid.text: $4 to $7 for 1,000 searches

services.catch: The text of a page is billed on top.

keys.name: EXA_API_KEY
keys.label: Exa search key
keys.why: The app uses it to search the web.
how: Go to dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys and sign in or make an account.
Create a key there.
Copy it and paste it into the app. Keep it private.

services.name: Brave Search
services.why: An index of its own, not Google's or Bing's.

free.text: $5 of credit a month, about 1,000 searches

paid.text: $5 for 1,000 searches

services.catch: It needs a card, and its terms do not allow keeping the results.

keys.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
keys.label: Brave Search key
keys.why: The app uses it to search the web; Brave's terms do not allow the results to be stored.
how: Create an account on the Brave Search API dashboard with your email and a password, then verify your email.
Open the Plans page, choose the Search plan and enter a card: it is asked even for free use.
Read the terms: the results may not be stored.
Open the API Keys section, click Add API Key and name it.
Copy the key and paste it into the app.

leftOut.name: Google's and Bing's search APIs
leftOut.why: closed to new customers or retired

leftOut.name: SerpApi
leftOut.why: three to five times the price

needs.note: Or the model provider's own web search, where you already have that key: more a search than these, plus the model's tokens.

needs.name: Files and backups off the server
needs.what: files and a second copy of backups, kept away from the app's server

services.name: Cloudflare R2
services.why: No charge for downloads, and a free allowance.

free.text: 10 GB stored and no charge for downloads

paid.text: $0.015 a GB a month past 10 GB

services.catch: Turning it on goes through a checkout, which may ask for a payment method.

keys.name: S3_ENDPOINT
keys.label: Endpoint
keys.why: It tells the app which web address to send files to.
how: Sign in to Cloudflare, open Storage & databases, then R2, then Overview, and finish the checkout that adds R2 to your account.
Free each month: 10 GB stored and set amounts of requests. Usage above that is billed, so expect to add a payment method.
On the R2 Overview page, find the address for the S3 API and copy all of it. It is also shown after you create an API token.
If you made your bucket in a special jurisdiction such as the EU, use the address for it, which has .eu before .r2.

keys.name: S3_BUCKET
keys.label: Bucket name
keys.why: It is the storage folder the app puts its files in.
how: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open R2 object storage and select Create bucket.
Type a name, keep the suggested location unless you need a particular one, and select Create bucket.
Copy the bucket name exactly as you typed it. New buckets are private unless you make them public.

keys.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
keys.label: Access Key ID
keys.why: It tells Cloudflare which key the app is using.
how: On the R2 Overview page, select Manage next to API Tokens.
Select Create Account API token, or Create User API token (a user token stops working if that user is removed).
Choose Object Read & Write, apply it to your bucket only, then create the token.
Copy the Access Key ID. Keep the page open, because you need the secret from it too.

keys.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
keys.label: Secret Access Key
keys.why: It is the password that goes with the Access Key ID.
how: Create the token as described for the Access Key ID.
On the confirmation page, copy the Secret Access Key and paste it into the app.
It is shown only once. If you lose it, create a new token.

services.name: Backblaze B2
services.why: The cheapest to keep more than a little in.

free.text: 10 GB stored

paid.text: $6.95 a TB a month; downloads free up to 3 times what you store

services.catch: No upload straight from a form in the browser.

keys.name: S3_ENDPOINT
keys.label: Endpoint
keys.why: It tells the app which web address to send files to.
how: Make a Backblaze B2 account, or sign in.
In the left menu under B2 Cloud Storage, click Buckets and make your bucket if you have none yet.
Find the Endpoint field of your bucket and copy it. It looks like s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com.
Type https:// in front of it when you paste it into the app.

keys.name: S3_BUCKET
keys.label: Bucket name
keys.why: It is the storage folder the app puts its files in.
how: Sign in, then in the left menu under B2 Cloud Storage click Buckets.
Click Create a Bucket, type a name (you are told if it is taken) and choose Private.
Click Create a Bucket and copy the name exactly.

keys.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
keys.label: keyID
keys.why: It tells Backblaze which key the app is using.
how: In the left menu under B2 Cloud Storage, click Application Keys, then Add a New Application Key. The master key will not work here.
Name it, choose your bucket under Allow Access to Bucket(s), and keep Read and Write.
If you chose one bucket, also tick Allow List All Bucket Names, which many apps need.
Click Create New Key and copy the keyID.

keys.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
keys.label: applicationKey
keys.why: It is the password that goes with the keyID.
how: Create the key as described for the keyID.
Copy the applicationKey at once and paste it into the app.
It appears only once. If you lose it, make a new key.

services.name: Hetzner Object Storage
services.why: One flat price, kept in Germany.

paid.text: €6.49 a month plus VAT, with 1 TB stored and 1 TB downloaded

services.catch: Billed while a bucket exists, even an empty one. New buckets in Helsinki are paused since 19 November 2026: choose Falkenstein or Nuremberg.

keys.name: S3_ENDPOINT
keys.label: Endpoint
keys.why: It tells the app which web address to send files to.
how: Note the location of your bucket: Falkenstein is fsn1 and Nuremberg is nbg1.
For Falkenstein the address is https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com
For Nuremberg, swap fsn1 for nbg1, and paste the address into the app without the bucket name.

keys.name: S3_BUCKET
keys.label: Bucket name
keys.why: It is the storage folder the app puts its files in.
how: Sign in to Hetzner Console (a new account needs your address and a payment method, and may be checked first) and open a project.
Click Object Storage in the left menu, then Create Bucket.
Pick Falkenstein or Nuremberg (new buckets in Helsinki are paused for now), a name nobody else at Hetzner uses, and Private.
Click Create & Buy now: it is paid for while the bucket exists, even empty.
Copy the bucket name exactly.

keys.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
keys.label: Access key
keys.why: It tells Hetzner which key the app is using.
how: In the same project as your bucket, click Security in the left menu.
Open S3 Credentials at the top and select Generate credentials.
Type a description, create them, and copy the access key from the top box.
By default these keys work for every bucket in that project.

keys.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
keys.label: Secret key
keys.why: It is the password that goes with the access key.
how: Generate the credentials as described for the access key.
Copy the secret key from the bottom box before you close the window.
It cannot be viewed again. If you lose it, generate new credentials.

leftOut.name: Amazon S3
leftOut.why: its account set-up and download fees

needs.name: A model, with your own key
needs.what: the model an app's AI features ask once it runs outside Hydor (inside Hydor it uses your models)

services.name: Anthropic
services.why: The one the AI features are written and tested against.

paid.text: Haiku 5.5 $0.10 in and $0.50 out, Sonnet 5.5 $2 and $10, a million tokens; paid in advance

services.catch: No region in the EU, and no embeddings.

keys.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
keys.label: Claude API key
keys.why: It lets the app ask Claude questions, billed to your account.
how: Sign in or create an account at platform.claude.com. This is billed apart from a Claude chat subscription.
It costs money: on the Billing page click Buy credits. Credits are paid in advance, expire after a year and are not refunded.
Open the API keys page and click Create key.
Name it, pick when it expires, link it to yourself and choose the Default workspace.
Copy the key right away, because it is shown only once. When it expires, make a new one.

services.name: OpenAI
services.why: One key for models and embeddings.

paid.text: GPT-6 Luna $0.10 in and $0.50 out a million tokens; from $5 of credit in advance

services.catch: Automatic top-up is on when you first buy: turn it off if you do not want it.

keys.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
keys.label: OpenAI API key
keys.why: It lets the app use OpenAI's models, billed to your account.
how: Sign in or create an account on the OpenAI platform. API use is billed apart from a ChatGPT subscription.
It costs money: in Billing, add payment details and buy credit in advance.
Auto-reload is on by default when you first buy. Turn it off if you do not want automatic charges. Credits expire.
Open the API keys page and create a new secret key.
Copy it right away, because the full key is shown only when you create it.

looks.say: is the secret key OpenAI shows once

services.name: Google Gemini
services.why: Paid like the others for an app that serves people in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, where its free tier may not be used; free to try elsewhere.

free.text: Limited models and use; not for people in the EEA, UK or Switzerland

paid.text: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite $0.30 in and $2.50 out a million tokens

services.catch: Elsewhere, Google may use what you send on the free tier to improve its products.

keys.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
keys.label: Gemini API key
keys.why: It lets the app use Google's Gemini models.
how: If the app serves people in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, set up billing: Google's terms allow only the paid tier there.
Open Google AI Studio's API keys page and sign in with a Google account. You must be 18 or older.
New users get a key made for them. Otherwise click Create API key, then copy the key.
On the free tier elsewhere, Google may use what you send to improve its products, and people may review it: send nothing private.
For paid use, click Set up billing and add a payment method: what is sent then is not used that way.

leftOut.name: OpenRouter
leftOut.why: a fee on every top-up and a catalogue too long to choose from (an app may still use it as another provider)

services.name: Stripe
services.why: The only one that also allows physical goods, services, donations and club fees.

paid.text: 2.9% + 30¢ a US card sale, no monthly fee

services.catch: Sales tax is yours to handle (Stripe Tax costs extra), and you can sign up only in some countries.

keys.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
keys.label: Secret key (test)
keys.why: It lets the app create checkouts and read what people have paid.
how: Create a Stripe account or sign in. Testing in a sandbox is available at once and moves no real money.
Click the account picker, choose Sandboxes, and create or open a sandbox.
Open the API keys page. Copy the sandbox's secret key, or click Create secret key and enter the code Stripe sends you.
Real payments later need your account set up and a live key; Stripe has no monthly fee but takes a fee on each payment.

looks.say: starts with sk_test_ while you try things, and sk_live_ for real money

not.say: That is the publishable key. Paste the secret key, which starts sk_.
That is a live key: real money would move. Here use a test key, which starts sk_test_.

keys.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
keys.label: Webhook signing secret
keys.why: It lets the app be sure a message about a payment really came from Stripe.
how: In the same sandbox, open the Webhooks tab in Workbench and click Create an event destination.
Choose Your account, then the payload style and events your app asks for, and continue.
Choose Webhook endpoint, and paste the app's public https address for Stripe messages.
Open the new endpoint, click Reveal secret and copy it. Live mode and each endpoint have their own secret.

services.name: Polar
services.why: Handles sales tax for software, courses and other digital things.

paid.text: 5% + 50¢ a sale, no monthly fee

services.catch: No physical goods, services or donations; new accounts wait 7 days for payouts.

keys.name: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN
keys.label: Organization access token (sandbox)
keys.why: It lets the app create checkouts and read your sales on Polar.
how: Open Polar's sandbox and make an account and organization there. It is separate from real Polar and moves no real money.
In your organization's Settings, open Access Tokens and click Create token.
Give it a name, an expiry date and the permissions your app asks for, then create it and copy it.
To sell for real, repeat on polar.sh: Polar reviews your account first (up to 14 days) and takes a fee per sale.

keys.name: POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET
keys.label: Webhook secret
keys.why: It lets the app be sure a message about a sale really came from Polar.
how: In the same sandbox organization, open Settings, then Webhooks, and click Add Endpoint.
Paste the app's public address for Polar messages, leave the format on Raw and select the events it asks for.
Save, open the endpoint, click Copy Secret and paste it into the app. Real Polar has its own, different secret.

services.name: Paddle
services.why: Handles sales tax for software companies, and has done so for long.

paid.text: 5% + 50¢ a sale

services.catch: Software only: no physical goods or donations, and a live account is approved first.

keys.name: PADDLE_API_KEY
keys.label: API key (sandbox)
keys.why: It lets the app read and manage your sales and subscriptions in Paddle.
how: Sign up for a free Paddle sandbox account at sandbox-vendors.paddle.com/signup. It is separate and takes no real money.
Go to Paddle, then My account, Settings, Authentication, open the API keys tab and click New API key.
Name and describe it, tick only the permissions your app needs, and set an expiry (90 days by default, one year at most).
Click Save and copy the key right away, because it is shown only once. Replace it before it expires.
Selling for real needs a live account that Paddle approves (website, identity, business if not a sole trader) and a new live key.

looks.say: starts with pdl_sdbx_apikey_ for the sandbox

not.say: That is a live key: real money would move. Here use a sandbox key.

keys.name: PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
keys.label: Webhook secret key
keys.why: It lets the app be sure a message about a sale really came from Paddle.
how: In the same sandbox account, go to Paddle, then Events, Notifications, and click New destination.
Set the type to URL, paste the app's public address for Paddle messages and choose the events it asks for.
Click Save destination, open it again and copy its Secret key. A live account needs its own destination and secret.

leftOut.name: Lemon Squeezy
leftOut.why: it closes on 31 March 2027, by its own page

needs.name: Sign-in with another account
needs.what: a "Sign in with …" button besides the app's own accounts

builtIn.say: A link sent by mail, and passkeys, need no service.

services.name: Google
services.why: Nearly everyone has an account, and plain sign-in needs no review.
services.catch: Press Publish app before real people sign in; Google may ask to verify before it shows your name and logo.

keys.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
keys.label: Client ID
keys.why: It tells Google which app is asking to sign a person in.
how: Open the Google Auth Platform in Google Cloud, sign in, and pick or create a project.
Fill in the Branding page (app name and contact details) and save. For people outside your organisation, choose External as the audience.
Open the Clients page, click Create client, and choose Web application as the application type.
Under Authorized redirect URIs add your app's address followed by the app's own callback path. It must start with https, except on localhost.
Click Create, then copy the Client ID. Copy the client secret now as well: it is shown only this once.
Before real users arrive, click Publish app. Google may ask for verification before showing your name and logo.

keys.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
keys.label: Client secret
keys.why: The app uses it to prove to Google that sign-in requests really come from it.
how: Create the Web application client as described for the Client ID.
Copy the client secret from the box shown right after you click Create, and keep it somewhere safe.
If you lose it you cannot view it again: open the client on the Clients page and rotate the secret to get a new one.

unconfirmed: What plain sign-in costs: no Google page read says it is free (the steps ask for no payment).

services.name: GitHub
services.why: For tools that developers use: the shortest set-up.
services.catch: Most people outside software have no GitHub account.

keys.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
keys.label: Client ID
keys.why: It tells GitHub which app is asking to sign a person in.
how: Sign in to GitHub, click your picture, then Settings, Developer settings, OAuth apps.
Click New OAuth App (it may read Register a new application) and enter the app's name and its web address as Homepage URL.
In Authorization callback URL enter your app's address followed by the app's own callback path.
Expire user access tokens is ticked by default; untick it only if your app says it cannot renew sign-ins.
Click Register application, then copy the Client ID.

keys.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
keys.label: Client secret
keys.why: The app uses it to prove to GitHub that sign-in requests really come from it.
how: Open your OAuth app under Settings, Developer settings, OAuth apps.
Next to Client secrets click Generate a new client secret.
Copy the new secret right away and keep it somewhere safe; if it is lost or leaked, generate a new one.

unconfirmed: What an OAuth app costs: no GitHub page read says it is free (GitHub's steps ask for no payment).

services.name: Microsoft
services.why: Where people sign in with their work accounts.

free.text: Entra ID Free, included with an Azure or Microsoft 365 subscription

services.catch: It needs an Azure subscription, and the free one asks for a credit or debit card. The app's secret lasts 24 months at most.

keys.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID
keys.label: Application (client) ID
keys.why: It tells Microsoft which app is asking to sign a person in.
how: You need an Azure account with a subscription: even the free one asks for a phone number and a bank card.
Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center, open Entra ID, then App registrations, and click New registration.
Enter a name people will recognise. Under Supported account types choose Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts, then Register.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the Overview page.
Open Authentication, click Add Redirect URI, choose Web, enter your app's address followed by its callback path, and click Configure.

keys.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET
keys.label: Client secret value
keys.why: The app uses it to prove to Microsoft that sign-in requests really come from it.
how: In the same app registration open Certificates & secrets, then Client secrets, and click New client secret.
Add a description, pick how long it lasts (24 months at most), and click Add.
Copy the text in the Value column straight away, not the Secret ID. It is never shown again after you leave the page.
Note the expiry date: sign-in with this secret needs a new one before then.

leftOut.name: Apple
leftOut.why: a yearly fee and a secret to renew twice a year, unless there is an iPhone app

needs.name: Text messages
needs.what: texts to people's phones, only when they are asked for

builtIn.say: Not offered unless asked for: each text costs money and US senders wait days to register; a code by mail has neither.

services.name: Twilio
services.why: The one to use when texts are wanted: well documented, with a sole-trader route in the US.

paid.text: About 1.2 to 1.3¢ a US text, about 11¢ one to Germany; a sign-in code 5¢ plus the text

services.catch: US senders register first, which takes days, and bots can run up your bill with texts.

keys.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
keys.label: Account SID
keys.why: It identifies your Twilio account when the app sends text messages.
how: Make a Twilio account. The trial only texts numbers you have verified.
Sign in to the Twilio Console.
On the Console home page, copy the Account SID.

looks.say: starts with AC, 34 characters in all

keys.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
keys.label: Auth Token
keys.why: It is the password the app uses to send messages from your account.
how: Sign in to the Twilio Console.
Open Workbench's Overview tab and find the Auth Token.
Click the eye icon to show it, or the copy icon. Keep it private: with it and the SID, others can send messages that you pay for.

keys.name: TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER
keys.label: Sender phone number
keys.why: It is the number your app's text messages are sent from.
how: Upgrade to a paid account (you add payment details) to send your own wording to any customer.
Open Phone Numbers, then Buy a number, choose one that can send texts and buy it (it is paid monthly).
To text US numbers from an ordinary 10-digit number, complete Twilio's A2P 10DLC registration, which has fees.
Copy the number with the plus sign and country code, with no spaces.

looks.say: starts with + and the country code

leftOut.name: Plivo, Telnyx and others
leftOut.why: no clearer fees for registration or Europe

needs.name: Seeing how the app is used
needs.what: counting visits and what people do

builtIn.say: The app's own counts, in its database: no cookies and no outside service.
builtIn.until: the person asks for an outside service

services.name: Umami
services.why: Free for one website, with no cookie banner to write for it.

free.text: 100,000 events a month for one website

paid.text: $20 a month

services.catch: Only one website free.

keys.name: UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID
keys.label: Website ID
keys.why: It tells Umami which website the visit counts belong to.
how: Sign up at Umami Cloud and take the Hobby plan.
Click Websites in the sidebar, then Add website, enter a name and your domain, and click Save.
Click Edit on that website and find the Tracking code section.
Copy only the long code in quotes after data-website-id.

looks.say: a UUID: a long code of letters and numbers in groups joined by hyphens

services.name: Plausible
services.why: The simplest reports, with no cookies.

paid.text: From $9 a month, after 30 days free to try

services.catch: No free tier.

keys.name: PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN
keys.label: Site domain
keys.why: It tells Plausible which website the visit counts belong to.
how: Create a Plausible account. There is a 30-day free trial with no card; after that it is a paid service.
On the Add a website page, type your domain in the Domain field, without https:// or www.
Use that same text here, exactly as you entered it in Plausible.

looks.say: a bare domain such as yourdomain.com, without https:// or www

leftOut.name: PostHog
leftOut.why: far more than a small app needs

builtIn.say: The app's own log, shown on its Run tab.
builtIn.until: the person asks for an outside service

services.name: Sentry
services.why: The standard, with a free plan that fits a small app.

free.text: 5,000 errors a month for one person

paid.text: $29 a month ($26 paid yearly)

services.catch: The free plan is for one person.

keys.name: SENTRY_DSN
keys.label: DSN
keys.why: It is the address the app sends its error reports to.
how: Make a Sentry account and take the Developer plan.
Open Projects, click Create Project, choose the platform your app is built with, name it, and click Create Project.
Copy the DSN shown in the setup guide.
To find it later, open the project's Settings, then Client Keys (DSN).

looks.say: a web address with a key before an @ sign and a project number at the end

services.name: Bugsink
services.why: More free events, the same libraries, and you can run it yourself.

free.text: 15,000 events a month for one person

paid.text: $16 a month for 75,000

services.catch: A small company's service.

keys.name: SENTRY_DSN
keys.label: DSN
keys.why: It is the address in your Bugsink that the app sends its error reports to.
how: Sign up for hosted Bugsink, or run it yourself on your own server.
Sign in and create a team if Bugsink asks. On your own install, change the default admin password.
On the Projects page, use the button at the top right to make a project, name it and save.
Copy the DSN from the Connect your Application instructions that appear.

looks.say: a web address pointing at your Bugsink, with a key before an @ sign

leftOut.name: PostHog
leftOut.why: far more than a small app needs

needs.name: Knowing it is up
needs.what: being told when the app stops answering

services.name: UptimeRobot
services.why: Free checks every few minutes, for business use too.

free.text: 50 monitors, checked every 5 minutes

paid.text: $12 a month paid yearly

services.catch: Checks every 5 minutes at most on the free plan.
setup: Create a free UptimeRobot account (no card needed): 50 monitors, checked every 5 minutes.
Sign in and click Add New Monitor.
Choose HTTP(s) and enter your app's web address; the friendly name fills in and you can change it.
Select who gets the alerts, such as your own email.
Set the checking interval and region, then click Create monitor.

leftOut.name: Better Stack
leftOut.why: its free tier is not for business use

needs.name: A domain
needs.what: an address of your own, like yourname.com

services.name: Cloudflare Registrar
services.why: At cost, with no jump at renewal, and an agent can set its DNS with one token.

paid.text: Domains at cost: the price depends on the ending, and renewal has no surcharge

services.catch: The domain uses Cloudflare's name servers.

keys.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
keys.label: API token (Edit zone DNS)
keys.why: It lets the app add and change your domain's DNS records so the address points to it.
how: To buy a domain: verify your Cloudflare email, open Register domains, search, click Purchase, add contact and payment details. It costs money yearly.
Open My Profile, then API Tokens, and click Create Token.
Pick the Edit zone DNS template and limit it to your own domain.
Click Continue to summary, then Create Token.
Copy the token immediately; it is shown only once.

looks.say: starts with cfut_ (or cfat_ for an account token); older tokens have no prefix

record.where: In Cloudflare, choose your domain, open “DNS” and then “Records”, and press “Add record”.
record.name: Name
record.then: Set “Proxy status” to “DNS only”, then press “Save”.

services.name: Porkbun
services.why: About the same price, without a Cloudflare account.

paid.text: A .com about $11.81 a year

services.catch: Turn on API access for each domain, or the key cannot change it.

keys.name: PORKBUN_API_KEY
keys.label: API Key
keys.why: Together with the secret key, it lets the app change your domain's DNS records.
how: Sign in to Porkbun, click Account at the top right, and choose API Access.
Name the key, choose its permissions, limit it to your domain if you like, and click Create API Key.
Copy the API Key, and copy the Secret Key at the same time.
Go to Domain Management, click Details beside your domain, and turn on API Access.

keys.name: PORKBUN_SECRET_API_KEY
keys.label: Secret Key
keys.why: It is the private half of the key pair that proves the app may change your domain.
how: Create the key as described for the API Key.
Copy the Secret Key before leaving the page; it is shown only once.
If you lose it, delete the key and create a new one.

record.where: In Porkbun, open “Domain Management”, press “Details” beside your domain, edit “DNS Records”, and press “Add Record”.
record.name: Host

needs.name: Keeping bots out of forms
needs.what: stopping programs from filling in the app's forms

services.name: Cloudflare Turnstile
services.why: Free with no cap, and most people solve nothing.

free.text: Unlimited checks and 20 widgets

services.catch: It needs a Cloudflare account (the site need not be on Cloudflare).

keys.name: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
keys.label: Sitekey
keys.why: It shows the bot check on your forms.
how: Sign in to Cloudflare, or make an account, and open the Turnstile page.
Click Add widget, give it a name, and add the domains your app runs on (up to 10).
Choose a region and a widget mode (Managed is one of them), then click Create. The region cannot be changed later.
Copy the Sitekey.

keys.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
keys.label: Secret key
keys.why: The app uses it to ask Cloudflare whether a visitor really passed the check.
how: Create the widget as described for the Sitekey, or open it from the Turnstile page.
Copy the Secret key.
Keep it private: it belongs only on the server, never in the page visitors see.

services.name: ALTCHA
services.why: No outside account and no cookie: your server does the check.

free.text: Open source and free

services.catch: A puzzle of work only, so weaker against a determined bot.

keys.name: ALTCHA_HMAC_KEY
keys.label: HMAC secret key
keys.why: The app signs each bot-check puzzle with it so that nobody can forge one.
how: No account is needed: the open-source library runs inside your own app.
It signs with a secret of your own (hmacSignatureSecret): let the app make one, or have a password manager make a long random one.
Keep it private on the server, and keep it the same so that puzzles already sent can still be checked.

leftOut.name: reCAPTCHA
leftOut.why: a Google Cloud project and a hard cap

services.name: Geoapify
services.why: Maps and address lookup under one free key, for business use too.

free.text: 3,000 credits a day, with a Powered by Geoapify line by the map

paid.text: $59 a month

services.catch: The free plan asks for its credit line to show.

keys.name: GEOAPIFY_API_KEY
keys.label: API key
keys.why: The app uses it to load maps and look up places or addresses.
how: Sign up at Geoapify's My projects page with email, Google or GitHub.
Click Create project; its first API key is made automatically.
Open the project's API keys tab and copy the key. It works at once.
On the free plan, show Powered by Geoapify beside the map.

services.name: A map file of your own
services.why: One file in your own storage: no outside service and no key.

free.text: The map data is free; you pay your storage

services.catch: You make and upload the file yourself, and looking up addresses needs something else.
setup: Download the free pmtiles tool from the go-pmtiles releases page on GitHub.
Pick a recent daily map build at maps.protomaps.com/builds. The whole world is about 120 GB, so cut out only your area.
Use the tool's extract command with the build's address and your area's corner coordinates; bboxfinder.com helps find them.
Check the result by dragging the new file onto the viewer at maps.protomaps.com.
Upload it to your own storage that supports range requests (Cloudflare R2 is recommended) and allow your app's address in its CORS settings.
Show an OpenStreetMap credit on the map; it is required.

leftOut.name: OpenStreetMap's own tiles for a busy site
